transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-29 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Rita Morales (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Cedarnova CTO), Priya Rao (Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Security), Elena Gomez (Product)

Summary (auto gen, maybe):
Cedarnova evaluating Redwood for an in-app recommendations feature and a customer support summarization pipeline. Primary interest in PLG quickstart to validate latency/cost, then evaluate Dedicated quota for production data residency and on-prem privacy. Security team flagged KMS and audit log format; wants SOC2 evidence and SSO flow.

Topics: quickstart credits, time-to-first-token (TTFT), hosted vs dedicated vs private, VPC/KMS, benchmarks, rollout plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Avery Chen from Redwood — I'll do a quick intro, Rita's our SE and she'll go into perf and bench stuff.
[00:18] Liam: Hi, thanks. Quick context: Cedarnova builds storefront personalization & a support summarizer for chat transcripts. We're running in GCP today and have a mix of Node and python microservices.
[00:33] Priya: And hi, main things for us are time-to-first-token for prototyping (we want to ship an internal POC in 2 weeks), plus data residency concerns for production.
[00:47] Rita: Totally makes sense. For the quickstart path you can use Redwood hosted API with free credits, get to first call in minutes. We usually see teams do an internal POC in under 3 days if they have sample prompts ready.
[01:10] Marcus: Quick question on data - if we use hosted, how long is payload retained, is it encrypted with our KMS, and can we review audit logs?
[01:25] Avery: Good Q — hosted has short retention by default, and for enterprise we provide options: Dedicated pools with isolation or Private VPC/on‑prem with KMS/HSM. We can share the retention policy doc. I'll add the SOC2 whitepaper. (slight overlap)
[01:45] Elena: Do you have a recommended path? Like start hosted for speed then flip to dedicated?
[01:52] Rita: That's our standard: start PLG/self-serve hosted for quick validation, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and VPC when you need data controls. Also we have automatic routing if you need fallbacks during rollout.
[02:10] Liam: For the POC, our latency SLO is 120ms p95 on short prompts (<128 tokens) — is that realistic on hosted?
[02:22] Rita: Depends on model choice. Lighter open models and shorter contexts can hit that; with Redwood's continuous batching and latency-first routing, p95 in the 80–150ms ballpark is possible for small models. For large context or bigger models you'll see higher numbers. We can benchmark.
[02:44] Priya: We also care about cost — if we go dedicated, what's the ballpark monthly for steady 200 qps?
[02:54] Avery: I'll be candid: dedicated reserve pricing depends on capacity and instance type. For 200 qps we'd need to map to GPUs and batch sizes; we'll send an estimate after Rita runs a micro-benchmark with your sample prompts.
[03:08] Liam: Ok. On infra, our infra team prefers VPC peering rather than a full on‑prem install — is that supported?
[03:18] Rita: Yes, VPC connections and private link options are supported for Private deployments. For Dedicated we also support customer-managed VPC with private control plane.
[03:30] Marcus: We're heavy on compliance. Does Redwood integrate with our KMS? We need envelope encryption using our KMS and audit logs in a particular JSON schema for SIEM ingestion.
[03:43] Avery: We do KMS integrations and HSM options on Private. Audit logs are available; I'll check the schema but we'll share a sample. Note: some of the hosted logs are aggregated — for strict SIEM ingestion you'd likely want Dedicated/Private.
[04:00] Elena: What's the path to production after POC? Example timelines.
[04:08] Rita: Typical flow: quickstart (hours-days) -> POC (1–3 weeks) -> Pilot with dedicated capacity (1–2 months) -> Prod rollout. But if you need compliance earlier, we can accelerate Private onboarding.
[04:22] Liam: Who would own the bench runs? We have some infra constraints and will need help setting up a harness.
[04:30] Rita: We'll partner — SE will run the initial runs with your sample set and share raw numbers and cost estimates. Then we'll hand off scripts so your engs can re-run locally or in your infra.
[04:45] Priya: For sample prompts, we have mix of product recs (few hundred tokens) and chat summaries (longer). Any guidance on prompt engineering for score parity?
[04:59] Rita: We'll send a short best‑practice doc. Also Redwood Optimize suggestions: quantization profiles and batching knobs that hit cost targets while preserving quality.
[05:15] Liam: Any known gotchas with KV cache or long convo state? We saw some vendors had degraded perf with large kv caches.
[05:26] Rita: We cache prefixes but big KV cache sizes can affect latency depending on model; there are tuning knobs. We'll test with your convo lengths.
[05:39] Marcus: Security follow-ups — SSO/SAML support, RBAC, and where keys live.
[05:46] Avery: SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning supported, RBAC in Console, and we can detail key storage options. I'll include docs and our SOC2 summary.
[06:00] Elena: For the in-app recommendations use-case — do you advise hosted inference during beta for lower ops?
[06:08] Rita: Hosted is easiest to start; lower ops and immediate scale with credits. If you get steady traffic and need predictable latency/cost, move to Dedicated. If you must control data residency, choose Private.
[06:22] Liam: Can you do A/B rollouts across model variants? Say start with a faster quantized model and fallback to full model on errors.
[06:31] Rita: Yes, rollouts and fallback policies are in the platform — canary, A/B, auto-fallback to smaller models. We'll demo that in the pilot phase.

[06:50] -- brief pause while Avery pulls up a slide deck --

[07:10] Avery: Sharing deck: drive.redwood/cs/cedarnova-quickstart (link in chat). This has step-by-step for credits and recommended playbook.
[07:25] Liam: Great. When you say "credits", is that per-token or a time-limited credit?
[07:34] Avery: Credits come as a dollar amount on the account to use with the hosted API; we also have trial tokens in some regions. We'll send the exact credit package for this trial.
[07:47] Priya: For the benchmark run, can we test both hosted and a small dedicated instance?
[07:53] Rita: Yes — we can spin a small dedicated pool for benching against your profiles; the SE bench will compare p50/p95, cost per token, and failover behavior.
[08:05] Marcus: One more on logs — we need IP address logs and request IDs for traceability.
[08:11] Avery: Those exist as part of audit logs; we'll include a sample export.

[08:30] -- mid-call swap of speaker labels, some crosstalk --

[08:55] Priya: If we start hosted and see model regressions after upgrading model versions, do you have quality monitoring?
[09:03] Rita: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We can attach your golden prompts so you get notified on output drift.
[09:18] Elena: What's the expected ops burden to run Dedicated? Are you managing infra or do we?
[09:26] Rita: For Redwood Dedicated we operate the pool but it's reserved for your account; config and autoscaling policies are collaborative. For Private/on‑prem you run infra and we provide control plane options.
[09:38] Liam: Ok good. We're on a tight timeline — internal deadline to have first POC demo on Oct 13. That gives us about two weeks.
[09:46] Avery: That's feasible if Priya can get sample prompts and Marcus can sign off on a minimal compliance checklist quickly. We'll prioritize the quickstart credits so you can hit first call fast.
[10:00] Marcus: On the compliance checklist, are there standard templates you provide?
[10:06] Avery: Yes — vendor security pack, SOC2, data processing addendum (DPA). I'll attach in the follow-up.
[10:18] Priya: For the bench scripts, we use a thin client in Node. Any SDKs?
[10:24] Rita: We have official SDKs for Node and Python and a curl-based quickstart. We'll send code snippets and a sample repo.
[10:35] Liam: Any red flags from your side about our stack? We're mainly GCP, but use some legacy services behind a NAT.
[10:43] Rita: NAT is fine — for VPC or private deployments we'll map connectivity. The only thing to watch is egress patterns if you plan on private data flows; SE will note network requirements.
[10:55] Elena: Budget question: if the POC looks good and we go to pilot, is there a way to do a short-term dedicated trial?
[11:03] Avery: Yes, we do pilot dedicated commitments with short-term reserved capacity for benchmarking. We'll include that option in the follow-up pricing note.
[11:15] -- closing minute recap --
[11:20] Avery: Recap: 1) We'll allocate credits and a quickstart checklist (Avery) 2) Rita will run bench harness comparing hosted vs small dedicated (Rita) 3) Cedarnova to supply sample prompts and compliance list (Priya/Marcus) 4) Redwood to send SOC2 + KMS integration notes (Avery). Any other items?
[11:38] Priya: No, that covers it. Thanks — we'll aim to get samples by Friday.
[11:44] Liam: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the bench results.
[11:48] Avery: Thanks all, chat summary + links in CRM and I'll follow up with timelines.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts/links mentioned: drive.redwood/cs/cedarnova-quickstart (deck), /redwood/security/SOC2-summary.pdf (will be sent), sample bench harness repo (link in follow-up).

Notes on transcript quality: speaker overlaps and a couple of mis-heard product names ("KV cash" noted once). Some timestamps approximate.
